subject: Token levers, traffic assumptions & close timeline — MAP cost checks
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@acmehealth.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: jason.lee@acmehealth.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + traffic profile — need unit econ sanity check

Hi Avery,

Attached is the first pass at the Mutual Action Plan we discussed. Important pieces for us to validate before we lock the pilot:

- Monthly traffic by endpoint (search vs. assistant). See tab "Traffic_Profile".
- Latency targets: 250ms p50 for assistant completions, 800ms p95 acceptable during peak.
- Qs around caching: we assume 30% prefix reuse for assistant messages; is that realistic?
- Batching assumptions: we modeled 8ms additional latency for micro-batching at 16 requests.
- Tokens per request: 1,200 input + 1,000 output average for the assistant flow.

Can you run a quick tokens-per-$ sanity check (tokens/$) and call out any conservative/defaults you recommend for caching and batching in the MAP? We need to validate economics before our procurement team drafts the SOW.

I attached ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx. Would prefer a short call tomorrow to go through top-line numbers.

Thanks,
Jordan Park
Senior PM, Acme Health
(attachment: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet))

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jason Lee <jason.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + traffic profile — need unit econ sanity check

Jordan — thanks for the draft and the traffic sheet. High level notes after a first pass; I attached a 1-page cost summary with conservative and baseline cases.

Top-line quick sanity: with the numbers you shared (avg tokens/request = 2,200), a baseline Redwood hosted model at $0.0008 per token equivalent (post-quantization, baseline) gives ~ $1.76 per request. With 100k monthly active requests that maps to ~$176k/mo (baseline).

Key levers and recommendations:
- Tokens/$: our recommended unit to show in the MAP is tokens per dollar at both model-inference and system-level. I included two bands: conservative (0.6x efficiency) and optimistic (1.2x).
- Caching (prefix/KV): your 30% reuse is reasonable for templated dialogs. We recommend validating with a 48-hour sample. If reuse is >=30%, effective token spend reduces proportionally; I modeled linearly in the sheet.
- Batching: for assistant requests, batching at 8–16 requests provides best tradeoff. We estimate added latency of ~6–12ms at 16 requests; your 8ms number is within range. Batching will reduce tokens/$ by ~18% in the baseline traffic mix in our model.
- Fallbacks & model variants: include a low-cost model for non-critical endpoints; that drops total spend by ~25% but adds routing complexity.

Open questions from our side for the MAP:
1) Peak concurrent requests (not just monthly) — we need 95th percentile concurrency to size dedicated capacity or burst policies.
2) Allowed tail latency for batched paths — if you require strict p95 < 300ms we may recommend smaller batch sizes during peaks.

Proposed next steps / timeline to align with your procurement:
- Tomorrow (Mon 2026-11-02) 10:00–10:30 PT: quick sync to validate the traffic sample and confirm concurrency numbers.
- By 2026-11-05: finalize MAP economics sheet and hand to procurement for SOW draft.
- By 2026-11-12: mutual sign-off on MAP and pilot kickoff.

Attaching: redwood_cost_summary_v2.pdf (two scenarios) and an updated MAP with notes (ACME_MAP_v1_review.xlsx).

Looking forward — happy to join procurement call if helpful.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com

(attachment: ACME_MAP_v1_review.xlsx (spreadsheet))

Subject: Re: MAP draft + traffic profile — need unit econ sanity check

Thanks Avery — this is helpful and in the right direction. A few clarifications before the call:

- Concurrency: p95 concurrent assistant requests is ~1,200 (we're comfortable sharing an anonymized trace).
- Latency tolerance: for typical clinical assistant flows we need p95 < 500ms, but for triage we can accept 800ms. We're ok with dynamic batching that adjusts by traffic intensity.
- Model fallback: procurement wants a conservative cost delta if we need to route to a higher-capacity host during peak incidents. Can you add a short note on worst-case monthly spend with no caching + full non-quantized model (worst case), and the delta if we add LRU prefix caching at 20% vs 40% reuse?

We can do the 10:00 PT sync; Jordan and I will be on. Can you invite and include a short agenda (15 min)?

Also, procurement flagged the need for an explicit SLO clause in the MAP regarding burst behavior and fallback routing. Can you provide Redwood's standard SLO language so procurement can evaluate?

-Jordan

Jordan / team — thanks for the quick responses and the concurrency detail, that helps a lot. Short answers and updated plan below.

1) Worst-case monthly spend (no caching, non-quantized): ~ $320k/mo (model + infra + networking buffer). I'll include the full calc in the MAP appendix.
2) LRU prefix caching impact: we ran the delta scenarios in the attached MAP appendix:
   - 20% reuse -> ~18% reduction in token spend
   - 40% reuse -> ~33% reduction in token spend
3) Dynamic batching recommendation: we will auto-scale batch sizes by measured p50 latency; smaller batches during peaks to hit p95 targets, larger during quiet windows. Expect averaging ~12% token savings vs no batching.
4) SLO language (draft): Redwood provides regional availability SLOs and a burst policy that routes overflow to lower-cost capacity tiers with notification and optional credits for latency SLO breaches. I'll paste a short excerpt in the MAP appendix and attach Redwood_SLO_excerpt.txt.

- 2026-11-12: MAP sign-off and pilot kickoff scheduling.
